Summary
- There is a coherent, interpretable difference here: Model B’s residual-stream difference (B − A) strongly points toward tokens about restaurants/cooking/cuisine and toward professional/academic/technical terms (e.g., dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, professional, technical, molecular).
- That signal is concentrated in the later transformer layers (layers ~16–25) and mainly in the very early token positions of the sequence (positions p0–p3/p4). That pattern implies a change that would affect the model’s immediate continuation choices (the first few tokens it emits).

Why I conclude that
- Repeated top logit-lens tokens across many high-norm (layer,position) cells: cooking/restaurant vocabulary appears consistently (Cook, Cooking, cooking, Restaurant, restaurant, culinary, kitchen, baking, Chef, oven, microwave, Cake), and academic/professional vocabulary also appears repeatedly (dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, honors, Professional, professional, technical, molecular, macroeconomic).
- These tokens are the top decodings for many of the highest-norm cells in the high layers (e.g., layers 18–25, positions 0–4), matching the L2 norm map which shows the largest differences in those same layers/positions.
- The concentration at late layers + early positions is typical of a change that shifts the probability mass of likely immediate continuations rather than a low-level lexical change.

What I cannot (reliably) assert
- I cannot definitively name a single training objective (for example “fine-tuned on recipes” vs “fine-tuned on résumés/LinkedIn”) because the signal mixes two related domains (food/restaurant vocabulary and academic/professional vocabulary). Either:
  - Model B was exposed more to culinary/restaurant/review-style data, or
  - Model B was exposed more to professional/academic/technical bios/texts, or
  - Some combination or correlated shift in data where those vocabularies co-occur (e.g., restaurant review sites that include author credentials, or a corpus of professional bios with culinary terms).
- The Patchscope readouts (actual continuations) are not provided here, so I can’t show concrete sampled continuations that would nail down which of those domain hypotheses is correct.

Short answer
- Evidence supports that Model B differs from A by biasing early-token residual activations toward culinary/restaurant and professional/academic/technical continuations, concentrated in late layers. The exact cause (which dataset or fine-tuning objective produced this) is plausible but not uniquely identifiable from the provided evidence.
